notes: Offline run (no API key): the loop is fully deterministic and issues zero LLM calls. Valid and invalid traces are mechanically near-indistinguishable offline (the AUROC~0.5 finding of SA-1/SA-3), so the mined obligation withholds credit from the whole 'no genuine test run' population; residual false-valids are traces that DID run a passing test yet still failed the hidden grader -- the irreducible shortcut/overfit core the semantic/integrity checker (--use-llm) targets.

Failure detection is witness-driven (avg.tex Sec. 3.11): a trace is tagged 'hidden_test_failure' iff its verification witness credited it valid while the recorded reward says it failed. The remediation is mined + gated + applied through the Step-8 primitives (mine_recurring_failures / score_config / accept_edit / apply_domain_spec_edit); the base agent is never changed.

The mined obligation only ever abstains (via its registered checker), so it can never turn a valid trajectory into a false 'invalid' -- it only moves an over-credited 'valid' to 'uncertain'. Negative transfer is therefore the (near-zero) new false-veto rate plus the valid coverage it costs; traces that ran a genuine test keep their credit (targeting).

J_hat trajectory contrasts the AVG offline loop vs. a frozen no-offline-loop config (ablation #5, avg.tex Sec. 4.5). This whole experiment is the 'no online loop' mode (ablation #6): the verifier is used purely as an outer-loop scoring function, the complement of SA-4's online intervention.
